generic_name: Estriol, Estradiol, Progesterone, and DHEA (Dehydroepiandrosterone) combination
purpose: This combination of hormones is used to help relieve symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, mood changes, low energy, and vaginal dryness. It may also help support bone health, mental clarity, and overall well-being. Doctors often prescribe this when a woman's natural hormone levels have dropped due to menopause or other hormonal imbalances.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes these hormones — estrogens (estriol and estradiol), progesterone, and DHEA — but levels drop as you age, especially during menopause. These medications simply replace or top up what your body is no longer making enough of on its own. By restoring more balanced hormone levels, your body can function better and many bothersome symptoms start to ease.
common_side_effects: Breast tenderness or swelling, bloating, mild nausea, headaches, mood changes or irritability, spotting or light vaginal bleeding, skin irritation at application site (if using a cream or patch), and water retention causing slight puffiness.
warnings: This combination hormone therapy is not safe for everyone. Women with a history of breast cancer, uterine cancer, blood clots, stroke, or heart disease should not use this without very careful discussion with their doctor. Long-term use of estrogens can slightly increase the risk of certain cancers and blood clots. Always tell your doctor about all medications and supplements you take, and never adjust your dose on your own. Regular check-ups and monitoring are very important while on this therapy.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very personalized and is usually based on your blood or saliva hormone levels and your symptoms. It is commonly prescribed as a cream, gel, capsule, or troche (dissolving tablet) applied or taken once daily, often at bedtime. Your doctor or compounding pharmacist will give you exact instructions tailored just for you — always follow their specific directions carefully.
